name: Cefoperazone + Sulbactam
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Sulbactam is cleared by the kidneys (about 84% in urine; half-life 6.9 to 9.7 hours in anephric patients), whereas cefoperazone is mainly excreted in bile. The label therefore caps sulbactam at 1 g every 12 hours at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 15–30 mL/min and 500 mg every 12 hours below 15, allowing extra cefoperazone alone for severe infections, and doses after dialysis. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Summary of product characteristics uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); thresholds 30 and 15.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 2 to 4 g/day of the 1:1 combination IV or IM in divided doses every 12 hours; up to 8 g/day in severe infection; maximum sulbactam 4 g/day (SmPC).
CrCl 15–30: maximum sulbactam 1 g every 12 hours (2 g/day of the 1:1 product). Extra cefoperazone may be given separately for severe infection (SmPC).
CrCl <15: maximum sulbactam 500 mg every 12 hours (1 g/day of the 1:1 product). Extra cefoperazone may be given separately (SmPC).

hd: Dose as for CrCl <15 (sulbactam maximum 500 mg every 12 hours); give the dose after dialysis, because hemodialysis markedly alters sulbactam kinetics (SmPC).
pd: No PD-specific data; dose as for CrCl <15.
crrt: No data in the SmPC. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Sulbactam: yes (hemodialysis significantly changes its clearance). Cefoperazone: half-life only slightly reduced (SmPC).
monitoring: Prothrombin time and bleeding (vitamin K deficiency; fatal hemorrhage reported), especially with poor intake, malabsorption, prolonged IV feeding or anticoagulants; give vitamin K if needed. Avoid alcohol during and for 5 days after. Kidney function with aminoglycosides. In combined hepatic and kidney impairment, cefoperazone no more than 2 g/day without level monitoring (SmPC).

pediatric.approved_ages: Children, including neonates (limited data in premature infants) (SmPC).
pediatric.usual_dose: 40 to 80 mg/kg/day of the 1:1 combination in 2 to 4 divided doses; up to 160 mg/kg/day in serious infections; maximum sulbactam 80 mg/kg/day. First-week neonates: every 12 hours (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney dosing in the SmPC; sulbactam is renally cleared, so reduce by analogy with adults. Specialist input.

adult: Source is an Indian generic's SmPC published by the Ethiopian FDA (regulator-hosted) rather than the Pfizer originator (Sulperazon), whose LPD is only on labeling.pfizer.com. Kidney rules match the originator wording; verify against PH insert.
PH products include 1:1 and 2:1 ratios; the caps are for sulbactam, so the combined-gram cap differs by ratio.
